answer: Agents booking island ferries or tundra freight get one vote per verified human operator. At a basalt-walled enrollment office, an identity check issues one private credential; all offices share a deduplicated registry. Each vote proves credential possession in zero knowledge and reveals an epoch-specific nullifier. The ledger rejects a reused nullifier, so 500 aliases cannot turn one credential into 500 votes. Extra influence requires distinct enrolled people; corrupt issuers and credential rental remain risks.
